summary: Penobscot County tower on High Cut Hill in Garland: built about 1940, replaced by a 65-foot tower in 1944; sources disagree on removal, about 1960 or 1971-72.

facts.design: 65-foot tower, erected fall 1944; the source's type wording ('wooden-modern steel ring connector') is unclear
facts.status_note: Gone; sources disagree on the removal year and none describes what remains on the hill

events.note: About 1940 per the Maine Memory photo record; the volunteer list gives the same date
New 65-foot tower erected in fall 1944 per the 1943-44 Forest Commissioner's report; the report does not say what happened to the earlier tower
Torn down about 1960 per the photo record and the Maine Historical Society photo inventory (as quoted by the volunteer list)
Register says removed between 1971 and 1972; disagrees with the about-1960 date

evidence.supports: fire towers spotted fires early to protect timber, lumber and paper industries
evidence.quote: It was especially important to spot fires quickly and get firefighting crews to the scene early to minimize damage and hence loss to the industries that depended on Maine's trees, especially lumber and papermaking.

evidence.supports: tower on High Cut Hill built about 1940
evidence.quote: Fire Tower on High Cut Hill built about 1940.

evidence.quote: In the fall of 1944 a new 65' wooden-modern steel ring connector tower was erected on High Cut Hill in Garland, Penobscot County.

notes_for_editor: Removal dates conflict: about 1960 (Maine Memory record and the Maine Historical Society photo inventory as quoted by the volunteer list) versus between 1971 and 1972 (former-lookout register). Left unresolved; a check with the Garland Historical Society or Maine Forest Service records would settle it. The 1944 entry's phrase 'wooden-modern steel ring connector' is unclear, so the design fact stays general. No sources found on staffing, fires or access. One search and about five page reads. Maine Memory record 8832 has a c.1950 photo that is a candidate for photos, but no image URL was captured and the record says images may not be reproduced without permission except for classroom use, so it is not added. Record coordinates come from the FFA list and were not checked against a second source. No corrections proposed.
